Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for full cardiorespiratory examination (auscultation), blood pressure, temperature, and repeat pulse assessment.
2. Provide patient with practice support team phone number to book the appointment today.
3. If examination confirms bacterial chest infection/pneumonia, start oral antibiotic (agent and dose to be decided after in-person review; no known drug allergies).
4. If symptoms fail to improve or exam raises concern, order chest X-ray to exclude alternative pathology (e.g., malignancy, pulmonary embolus).
5. Safety-net advice: seek urgent care (999/ED) if breathlessness worsens, hemoptysis increases, develops high fever, or feels acutely unwell.
6. Review medication history (Methotrexate for SLE) during face-to-face visit to ensure no interaction with proposed antibiotics.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaints: sudden onset (today) right-sided pleuritic back pain on deep inspiration, shortness of breath, two episodes of hemoptysis, subjective fever.  
• Associated symptoms: awareness of heartbeat, fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks.  
• Past medical history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).  
• Medications: Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented; last dose taken this morning.  
• Allergies: None known (medication or other).  
• Social: Non-smoker; office desk job; lives alone in a flat; owns a cat. No recent long-haul flights. No personal or family history of thromboembolism.

Objective:
• Pulse (patient-counted): ~66–74 beats/min, regular.  
• Capillary refill: brisk (<2 s).  
• Oropharynx: visualized via video, no abnormality noted.  
• Cervical lymph nodes: self-palpated, no enlargement reported.  
• No other vitals or physical findings available via remote exam.

Investigations: None performed during video consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute pleuritic chest pain with hemoptysis
   - Assessment: Suspected lower respiratory tract infection / pneumonia.
   - Differential: Pulmonary embolism, malignancy (less likely given acute onset), viral infection including COVID-19.
   - Investigations planned: In-person auscultation, vitals; consider chest X-ray and blood tests if indicated.
   - Treatment planned: Empiric oral antibiotic if bacterial infection confirmed; symptomatic care; safety-net instructions.
   - Referrals: Same-day GP clinic review; possible radiology referral if persistent symptoms.

2. Fatigue and palpitations
   - Assessment: Likely secondary to current infection; monitor.
   - Differential: Anemia, medication side effect, SLE flare.
   - Investigations planned: Basic observations during face-to-face visit; further work-up only if persists.
   - Treatment planned: Reassurance; address underlying cause after assessment.
   - Referrals: None at this stage.

3. Existing SLE on Methotrexate
   - Assessment: Stable; no flare symptoms reported.
   - Treatment planned: Continue Methotrexate as prescribed; review for interactions with any future antibiotics.
   - Referrals: None.

Quality checks:

● Missing elements: Objective vitals (temperature, BP, respiratory rate, SpO₂); medication dose/frequency; comprehensive systems review.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient gave two different names (“Tracy Chapman” vs “Doris”) – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor background repetitions but clinically intelligible.
